runs.content: Shell plc (LSE, 3,657p) was bought as the day's energy sector-rotation pick. Renewed US–Iran tensions lifted oil and made energy one of only a few gaining sectors in a −0.8% S&P session with the 10Y yield at 5.24%. Shell closed at a 52-week high yet trades ~9x forward earnings, has a buyback running to 23 Oct, and diversifies the book beyond CVX/COP/OXY. NOC was exited as a capacity trim (−7.70%, −$77) to hold the book at 35 positions. No stop/T1/T2 triggers; RIGL is $0.97 from T1. Portfolio net P&L: +$1,554 (+2.29% on $68,000).

Deere & Company picked up at today's close ($690.46) — Baird upgraded to Outperform ($800 PT from $640), corn/soy futures +22% YTD (genuine ag-cycle tailwind), Q3 FY26 beat-and-raise (rev $12.61B, EPS $5.10); all-time-high Dow 30 momentum name entered on a broad market rally (S&P +0.51%, Dow +0.93%) despite the 10Y Treasury yield hitting 5.18%, highest since the financial crisis. OTIS was exited discretionarily (−8.42%, −$84) on a genuine thesis break — Otis cut its FY26 operating-profit outlook alongside a Q2 revenue beat and kept grinding to fresh 52-week lows through September — freeing capacity for DE and holding the book at 35 open positions. NOC (−6.84%, no Burry conflict) is now the weakest continuing position. Portfolio net P&L: +$1,622 (+2.42% on $67,000).
